where: the 'Copy command' / 'Check again' pair and the 'Checked 6:41 pm' reply beneath them, immediately under the gcloud block, at the bottom edge of the fold
finding: The remedy came up out of the basement and stopped exactly on the sticky tab bar, which is the one place on this screen it must not rest. Two costs follow. First, the re-check reports into nowhere: the whole point of r02's change was that during the thirty-to-a-hundred-and-twenty seconds an IAM grant takes to propagate the honest answer is 'still no', so the reply has to be legible when it is identical — and in the only state where anyone presses that button, the reply is 100% behind opaque chrome at rest. Dana taps the visible sliver of 'Check again', the page does not visibly change, and she is back to 'checked again, still refused' versus 'the button did nothing'. Second, the bottom 55% of both buttons overlaps the navigation bar, so a tap aimed at the middle of what looks like a button leaves the page entirely — she loses the diagnosis and the command and has to come back through the account menu. This is not the r02 finding restated: that one was 'the remedy is 106px below the fold, one flick away'. It moved, and the new position is worse than below the fold, because below the fold nothing pretends to be tappable.
evidence: 390x844, touch. 'Copy command' x=16-168, y=756-800; 'Check again' x=180-308, y=756-800; both 44px tall. The tab bar is fixed at y=776-832, bg-ink-950/95 with a backdrop blur, so 24px of each 44px button (55%) is covered and the labels clip mid-glyph in the fold frame. The tab targets underneath are 78px wide: 'Copy command' spans Check in (0-78), Insights (78-156) and part of Events (156-234); 'Check again' spans Events, Students (234-312). Gap between two adjacent targets with different consequences: -24px. The aria-live reply box is y=808-840 with its 16px line at 808-824 — entirely inside the bar's band. In the healthy state the same reply sits at y=595 and is perfectly visible, so the element is only invisible in the state that needs it.
direction: Reorder inside the block rather than trying to win vertical space: verdict, explanation, then the two buttons and their reply, then the `pre`. The command is the only thing here that is reference material you scroll to and copy rather than aim at, so it is the safe thing to let pass under the bar; the button that must be pressed twice and the line that answers it are not. That puts the buttons around y=634 and the reply around y=686 with no content deleted, which is what r02's 'arithmetic cannot be won' objection was measured against. Nothing in the constraints blocks it — this is a layout order change, not a copy or product change.

where: 'Sign out' in the identity block, right-aligned at the top of the sheet, and the single 'Kiosk' row directly below it
finding: The ordering fault from r02 is closed — Sign out is no longer a full-width slab under the thumb, it is a 74px control attached to the account it acts on, and the destination owns the reachable band. What survives is one column of overlap. The bottom-most row on the screen is the row a thumb undershoots, because a thumb reaching the bottom edge arcs and lands short; the region it lands in is the 9px gutter and the strip above it, and in the right-hand 74px of that strip — precisely where a right thumb travels — is Sign out. Everywhere else in that strip is inert identity text, so a miss is harmless for 79% of the row's width and ends the evening for the other 21%. On the admin build this cannot happen: three destination rows separate the two.
evidence: 390x844, touch, counselor sheet: Sign out x=308-382, y=731-775 (74x44); Kiosk x=0-390, y=784-832 (390x48). Vertical separation 9px plus a 1px rule. The two share the x-band 308-382. The counselor's sheet has exactly two interactive elements, so there is no cushioning row; the admin sheet at the same measurements has Sign out at y=635 with Kiosk (688), Team (736) and Settings (784) below it.
direction: Either add 8-12px below the identity block so the gutter is wider than a typical aiming error, or move Sign out off the thumb's column — left-aligned under 'Signed in as' it is still attached to the identity and no longer sits above the one row the whole journey depends on. Either is a spacing change inside a surface that is otherwise now right.
